title: Nirenberg–Treves estimates and square-root commutators
source_hypothesis: Arbitrary complex Hilbert space; B bounded, fixed and self-adjoint; A(t) bounded, nonnegative, self-adjoint and norm-continuous. The commutator product is bounded by M/10. Compactly supported C1 curves satisfy the solution estimate for TM<1/2 and the positive energy estimate for every T.
completed_component_scope: An evolution with a nonnegative operator multiplying a fixed self-adjoint operator need not itself be positive. The obstruction is their failure to commute. We bound that obstruction through two ordinary commutators, then obtain both a small-time solution estimate and a positive energy estimate. Every operator acts on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space; no finite-dimensional reduction or spectral gap is assumed.
reviewed_arguments: All three numbered Section 26.8 results are proved for arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces, including nonseparable spaces, continuous spectrum and a nontrivial zero space. The solution estimate requires TM<1/2; the positive energy estimate has no small-time condition.

The bounded-operator space and closed-subspace orthogonal projections are constructed explicitly. Exact CT:T1 and CE:H4–H5 supply the adjoint norm identities and actual Banach-valued integration. Historical local provider copies are not substituted for the verified current payload.

A norm-convergent binomial series constructs positive square roots. The coefficient recurrence, sum one, squared identity, commutation and positivity of products of commuting positive operators are proved.

The full Bernstein coefficient identity proves polynomial positivity, then contractivity. The mean and variance estimates prove uniform approximation. These give the continuous functional calculus by norm limits without an assumed spectral-measure theorem.

Closures of the positive and negative ranges give the two sign subspaces. The common orthogonal complement is exactly the kernel. The zero space is assigned to the minus projection, and all commutations and half-derivative bounds are proved.

A subtracted resolvent formula is absolutely convergent in operator norm, including at zero spectral value. Pairing the two scalar halves and evaluating a quartic integral gives the exact normalization; no contour assertion is left unproved.

The resolvent commutator has both the small-time and large-time norm bounds. The arbitrary splitting-point estimate and its optimized consequence are stated separately. All zero-factor cases are handled without division.

Jacobi and two applications of the one-root estimate give 32/pi-squared. An exact rational lower bound for pi proves this is smaller than 10/3, completing the double-root commutator with the original constant.

The self-adjoint double commutator isolates the positive diagonal form and bounds each opposite-sign term. Both time derivative signs and the two affine weights are explicit. Their exact error coefficient gives 4T/(1-2TM).

The half-derivative energy is retained before absorption. The weights 2T minus/plus t, mixed-sign Cauchy–Schwarz and the final two square inequalities give constants 18 and 2 without a small-time assumption.

Three complete examples cover a noncommuting positive matrix family, continuous spectrum with a separate zero space, and the commuting case. The original figure depicts the actual commutator, strict time threshold and amplification factor with exact domains.
